newsitem.title: USA: Texas mother did nothing to save sons - police.
newsitem.headline: Texas mother did nothing to save sons - police.

text.p: A Texas mother accused of killing her two sons ignored police requests to help save the boys while they lay dying of stab wounds, a police officer testified Tuesday.

The officer, David Waddell, said in the trial of Darlie Routier that she appeared more interested in telling him about her fight with an intruder who she said killed the boys than in doing anything to help them.
"I instructed her to get a towel to put on the child's back and she kept telling me about the fight," Waddell told a jury of seven woman and five men.
Routier, 27, is accused of stabbing to death sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, as they slept in the living room of their comfortable home in Rowlett, Texas, near Dallas on June 6.
Prosecutors said in opening arguments on Monday that she was angry because she felt fat and the family's business was floundering.
Routier has said the murderer was a male intruder, dressed in dark clothes and a baseball cap, who broke into her home, stabbed the boys and her when she tried to intervene, then escaped.
But prosecutors accused her of inventing the story about an intruder and of stabbing herself in the neck and shoulder to back up her story.
Waddell, who was the first officer on the scene, said Routier was hysterical when he arrived and told him the intruder was still in the garage. The two children were lying on the floor.
Waddell said he told husband Darin Routier to apply pressure to the wounds of one of the boys, which he did, but that his requests for Darlie to help the other child went unheeded.
"He was making sounds like he was trying to breathe," Waddell said of the boy.
No intruder was found by police. Waddell told the court that, once paramedics arrived and began working on the two boys, Routier never asked about her sons' condition.
During cross examination by defence attorney Doug Mulder, transcripts from Routier's conversation with the emergency operator were read in which she urged the boys not to die.
"Hold on, baby, hold on," Routier said. "They're dead, oh my god, they're dead."
Darin Routier was not charged by police and insists his wife is innocent. If convicted, Darlie Routier could be given the death sentence.
State district judge Mark Tolle moved the trial to Kerrville, 80 miles northwest of San Antonio, Texas, because of intense publicity for the case in Dallas.
